# Gajjala variants + "next Gajjala" among USIC champions: SYNTHESIS (2026-11-01)

Built only from the sweep files and deep reads in this folder. Every number below carries the URL it came from. Rules are written as **close paraphrases with timestamps**, not long verbatim quotes (copyright limit). Open the timestamp to hear his exact words. Nothing here has been implemented or traded. Promotion, thresholds and gaps are **HIS CALL**.

**Bottom line:**
- **Nobody has published a tested "modified Gajjala" with results.** The closest are F4VS's tweaks, and his own live R logs are mixed to negative.
- **No USIC champion other than Gajjala and Minervini has a free-complete playbook** once the skeptics' refutations are applied.
- **Best free-partial: Martin Luk** (2025 champion, +969.8%). He sells nothing, and both skeptics found no paywall. He drops a grade only because his selling and exposure rules are, in his own words, not hard rules.

### A3. Verdict: is any modification worth a paper test? (Named, not decided. HIS CALL.)

**No third-party modification comes with tested results.** The only R numbers are F4VS's own later lane, which never names GG and is mixed to negative (Nov 2025 −5.43R, Jul 2026 −4.7R).

The modifications concrete enough to test as a **paper variant of the existing Gajjala lane** are:
1. **F4VS MIL time cut**: the premarket-high break must happen by 11:59 am, plus a float <100M cap (https://retailtradersrepository.substack.com/p/finding-an-edge-database-and-playbook-morning-intraday-long-setup).
2. **F4VS volume-spike exclusion**: skip a 10x prior-candle volume spike; 2-3x is fine (https://retailtradersrepository.substack.com/t/goverdhan-gajjala).
3. **GG's own first-hour-worst / 11 AM + 5 PM evidence** (https://x.com/gov_gajjala/status/1753343067846058314). This ties into the open after-hours-window HIS CALL from the 10-29 re-look.

Base-rate warnings on gap-ups: SmallCapLab measured 67.7% of ≥45% premarket gappers closing below the open, with half of highs-of-day in by 9:45 (https://www.smallcaplab.com/research). FennEdge (snippet only) found 65.3% of 20%+ openers closing below the open (https://fennedge.ai/glossary/gapper). The TraderLion snippet stats (750 trades, 31% wins, +8.55% / −4.06%) put fixed-size expectancy at about −0.04R (https://traderlion.com/investing-champions/2023-us-investing-champion/). Any GG variant needs the strategy-lab treatment (pre-registered, out-of-sample, placebo) before it touches paper. **Whether to test #1, #2 or #3 is HIS CALL.**

## D) RECOMMENDATION

**No champion other than Gajjala and Minervini has a free-complete playbook** after the refutation rule is applied. The best free-partial is:

### Martin Luk (2025 USIC $20k+ Stock winner +969.8%; 2026 leader +785.8% through Sep 30)

**Why him, in three lines:**
1. **He is the only exposed champion.** He sells nothing (his X bio says so), both skeptics found no paywall, and his rules are in his own voice in free podcasts, streams and a guest post. He drops a grade only because his selling and exposure rules are self-admittedly discretionary.
2. **He is the closest to GG mechanically.** Gap-up and top-mover scans, an intraday 1/5-min previous-bar-high trigger, a low-of-day stop, stops of 5% or less, and a low win rate with high R. This reuses Cheetah's Gajjala minute plumbing, with a daily EMA/AVWAP layer and multi-day holds added.
3. **He is the only candidate with independent point-in-time backtests, and they are sobering.** Close-confirm variant: CAGR 12.1%, Sharpe 0.83 (the same as QQQ), max drawdown −13%. His **literal morning trigger is flat to negative after spreads**: rootchunhe CAGR −2.2%, 13% winners; zongfan2 replica −58.3%, max drawdown −87.6%. So this is a **paper/shadow lane only, measured first**.

### Rule set (close paraphrase; per-rule URL and timestamp)

**Universe / scans**
- U1. Mainly stocks with ADR >5% in hot themes ("not a hard rule"). https://tradingresourcehub.substack.com/p/martin-luk-283-usic-2024-key-lessons
- U2. Three scans: potent (yesterday's top performers), pre-market (gap-ups), and leader (top movers over 30 days, run on weekends). Same URL.
- U3. Watchlist tiers by EMA order: Lead 9>21>50, Lag 9<21<50, Mediocre in between; plus a small-cap list for <$5B. Same URL.
- U4. Premarket screen: cap >$100M, 10D avg volume >500K, price×volume >$50M, 1W volatility >3.5%, sorted by premarket %. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iMBI3ZcQ6sU (~1:17:44); frames checked at https://martinluk.com/screeners/index.html
- U5. Leader screen: cap >$100M, 10D avg volume >500K, 1W price×volume >$300M, sorted by 1M %. Same.
- U6. Potent screen: price > EMA50, price ≥ EMA21, cap >$100M, 1W volatility >3.5%, price×volume >$50M, change from open outside ±0.5%, sorted by % change. Same.
- U7. Moving the dollar-volume floor toward $100M and filtering biotechs out. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iMBI3ZcQ6sU (1:15-1:22)
- U8. Within a theme: fastest movers, strongest RS, tightest name, highest dollar volume. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw (18:45; 3:16:37-3:18:44)

**Entry**
- E1. Pullback trades wait for at least the daily 9 EMA. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw (49:58)
- E2. After a fast flush into support at the hourly 9/21 EMA, buy the first break of the previous bar's high on the 1, 5 or 15-min chart. Same video (1:56:39)
- E3. Use the 1-min candle in the first 15 minutes, then the 5-min candle from 15 to ~60 minutes after the open. Same video (1:57:23)
- E4. No chase: if the stock is already up more than 3% from the low of day, skip it. Same video (24:37)
- E5. Wait for a 5 or 15-min candle breakout after support holds; do not buy the dip on the way down. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tx321OQ8iD0 (1:49:06)
- E6. Opening-range high = take-out of the first 1-min candle high, stop at the LOD; use the 1-min chart until the first 5-min candle forms. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (38:25-40:26)
- E7. Prior-day-high breakout after an inside day. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (36:11)
- E8. Best pullback: the first one in a base with higher lows, where the 9/21/50/150 EMA, anchored VWAP, prior high and gap coincide. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw (1:10:01, 1:17:34, 2:04:13)

**Initial stop**
- S1. Stops of 1-5% (mostly), never more than half the ADR; over 80% of 2024 stops were under 3.5%; hard stop placed as soon as the order fills. https://tradingresourcehub.substack.com/p/martin-luk-283-usic-2024-key-lessons
- S2. Maximum 5%; rarely wider than 3% or 2.5%. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw (18:10)
- S3. Stop at the LOD about 60-70% of the time; otherwise the low of the breakout bar or the previous bar. Same video (1:58:18)
- S4. If entry-to-LOD is more than 5%, use the 5-min entry candle's low. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (38:02)

**Exits**
- X1. Partial sells into strength at 3R or 5R, or when really extended on lower timeframes (1-hour). https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw (2:27:34)
- X2. Trims of about 15% each; close the rest on the first close below the 9 EMA. Same video (2:29:05); first trim 15-20% (2:56:11)
- X3. Trims of 10-15% once profit is over 3R; trim when a position grows past 35% of the account. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (40:48-41:32)
- X4. Early in a strong trend, trail on the 21 or 50 EMA instead of the 9. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (42:46-43:27)
- X5. Parabolic exit: sell all when intraday dollar volume passes 50% of the prior day's by mid-session, the prior day's dollar volume was a 52-week high, and price is near weekly resistance. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (1:17:17-1:18:44)
- X6. 2024 rule: a 9 EMA trailing-stop sell rule. https://tradingresourcehub.substack.com/p/martin-luk-283-usic-2024-key-lessons

**Sizing**
- Z1. Risk per trade: about 0.5% (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw 16:09); 0.5-1% in 2024 (Substack); about 0.3% now (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yvaMXQfOEWI 2:13:26, ambiguous caption).
- Z2. Positions of about 25-30%. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw. Worked example: $10k × 0.5% = $50 of risk; $50 / 2.5% stop = $2,000 position (3:03:50).
- Z3. Gross exposure at most 280% long (41:14); normally 3-4 positions, up to 11 at peak (43:49).
- Z4. Never raise risk in a drawdown. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yvaMXQfOEWI

**Market**
- M1. Daily read of QQQ and IWM; be aggressive during QQQ pullbacks, not when it is extended; breadth = count of Lead vs Lag watchlist names. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKNEJA5r8zw (3:47:19-3:50:49)
- M2. Example, not a threshold: QQQ almost 2% above its 9 EMA → no aggressive longs and no chasing breakouts. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=297D7gVsLY4 (1:02:41)
- M3. Indices with the 9 EMA under the 21 = unfavourable for longs; skip setups when indices bounce into a declining 21/50 EMA. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lS9zbnLi1Gg (1:57:39-1:58:18)

### Gaps needing HIS CALL (no number invented)

1. **Entry implementation.** His literal morning 1/5-min trigger measured −2.2% CAGR with 13% winners after spreads. The rootchunhe 15:55 close-confirm proxy measured 12.1% CAGR, Sharpe 0.83, roughly equal to QQQ. Options: one of them, or both as paper variants (https://github.com/rootchunhe/martin-luk-backtesting).
2. **Risk per trade:** 0.3%, 0.5% or 0.5-1%. He has used all three over time.
3. **Position cap:** a 35% cap (2024 rule; Kyna's Jan 2026 post) or no cap (2025, VKNEJA5r8zw 16:37-18:02).
4. **Gross exposure / margin:** up to 280% in his account; what the paper account allows.
5. **Exit precedence** among 3R/5R trims, the 9 EMA close, the 21/50 EMA early trail and the parabolic rule. He has no hard sell rule, and "really extended on the 1-hour" is undefined.
6. **"Really fast flush"** into hourly EMA support has no number.
7. **Anchored VWAP anchor choice** (base swing high/low, gap day, 250-day high per rootchunhe) is not specified.
8. **Market gate as a hard rule.** Whether M3 (index 9<21) becomes a gate, and what QQQ distance from its 9 EMA blocks longs (M2 is one example only).
9. **Potent-screen industry exclusion list** is not visible in the frames.
10. **Earnings blackout** of 5 days ~95% of the time comes from the fan FAQ only; it needs confirming from the stream.
11. **Max hold:** none stated by Luk; rootchunhe used 15 days (third-party).
12. **Shorts:** in or out of scope (his short rules: https://tradingresourcehub.substack.com/p/martin-luk-study-process).
13. **Exposure building and watchlist tier overrides** are by his judgment, with no rule.
14. **Unread primary:** his May 2025 X post on pullback entry tactics (cited by him at VKNEJA5r8zw 1:00:15).
15. **Promotion:** results are regime-bound (the ten best trades = 111% of P&L; 2025 is about a third of it; the 9 EMA is a fragile peak; no clean out-of-sample period). Any lane goes through the strategy-lab prereg (OOS + placebo + DSR) and **paper only on HIS CALL**.

**Runner-up: David Ryan (free-partial).**
- Every trade rule is free in his own voice: buy at the pivot above ~90% of the base, at most 5% past it; 3-8% stop; staircase trail; 5% → 10% → 20% pyramid; Ants 12/15.
- But the scan needs paid IBD data, his market read uses undisclosed indicators, and the horizon is weeks to months.
- Its natural home is an extension of the SEPA stack, not a Gajjala-like lane.
